processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: A 20 kg ingot of the Fe–10Mn–10Al–0.7C steel was prepared by vacuum induction melting method.
The ingot was heated to 1200 °C prior to forging.
The ingot was forged to a forging blank with cross section of about 40 mm × 60 mm.
The forging blank was homogenized at 1200 °C for 1 h before hot rolling.
The forging blank was hot-rolled to a plate of 3 mm thickness, with the finishing rolling temperature around 880 °C.
The hot-rolled plate was water quenched to about 300 °C, giving the reference HR state before annealing.

structures.overall_structure: Hot-rolled (HR) specimen: typical banded microstructure, very inhomogeneous, composed of large α phase areas and γ phase areas; coarse ferrite formed during the early stage of solidification is observed; κ-carbide present along ferrite/austenite (α/γ) and ferrite/ferrite (α/α) boundaries.

phases_present.morphology: coarse ferrite formed during the early stage of solidification; elongated dark bands (typical banded structure)

defects.type: dislocations inherited from the hot rolling process

grain_structure.texture: typical banded structure presented in RD–ND plane, bands elongated along RD

phases_present.morphology: large continuous α phase area (with some γ phase or κ-carbide dispersed)
large continuous γ phase area (with some α phase or κ-carbide dispersed)
particles decorating α/γ and α/α boundaries (SEM, Fig. 3(c))

precipitates.coherency: κ-carbide peaks not seen in XRD of the HR specimen, probably due to low volume fraction of κ-carbide or the coherency of κ-carbide and α matrix

structures.overall_structure: Equilibrium phase constitution of the Fe–10Mn–10Al–0.7C steel calculated by Thermo-Calc predicts ferrite (α), austenite (γ) and κ-carbide (κ); ferrite forms first during solidification, then austenite by peritectic reaction; κ-carbide appears by eutectoid reaction γ → α + κ below ~823 °C.

phase_interfaces.coherence: κ-carbide along α/α boundaries; coherency with α matrix suggested as a reason κ XRD peaks are absent in HR

interfaces.phase_evolution: In the hot-rolled specimen κ-carbide is present along α/γ and α/α boundaries (SEM, Fig. 3(c)); κ-carbide peaks are absent from the HR XRD pattern, probably due to the low volume fraction of κ-carbide, or the coherency of κ-carbide and α matrix.
interfaces.interface_notes: EDS confirmed the phases: α phase is Al-rich, γ phase is Mn-rich and C-rich, while κ-carbide is Mn-rich and Al-rich.

characterization_methods.key_findings: In the hot rolled (HR) specimen, peaks of κ-carbide are not seen, probably due to the low volume fraction of κ-carbide, or the coherency of κ-carbide and α matrix. α and γ related reflections are present in all specimens.

characterization_methods.purpose: microstructure examination of the hot rolled specimen
characterization_methods.key_findings: RD–ND plane shows a typical banded structure with coarse ferrite formed during the early stage of solidification; RD–TD plane shows a very inhomogeneous microstructure with large α phase area and γ phase area.

characterization_methods.technique: field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FE-SEM) with energy dispersive spectrometer (EDS)

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: specimens mechanically polished and etched by 8% Nital

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Equilibrium calculation of phase fractions vs temperature (above 550 °C) for the Fe–10Mn–10Al–0.7C composition
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: The calculated κ-carbide dissolution temperature (~823 °C) is lower than the actual dissolution temperature measured between 850 °C and 900 °C, attributed to thermodynamic calculation error and the difference between equilibrium and disequilibrium. Calculated fractions are atomic-based whereas XRD-measured fractions are volume-based.

analytical_models.equation_role: Predict fractions of ferrite (α), austenite (γ) and κ-carbide (κ) as a function of temperature
analytical_models.model_note: Ferrite expected to form first during solidification, austenite by peritectic reaction; κ-carbide appears by eutectoid reaction γ → α + κ below 823 °C.

unmapped_findings: The chemical composition of the hot rolled steel was measured to be 10.4 wt.% Mn, 9.7 wt.% Al, 0.70 wt.% C, and Fe balance (b0016).
The measured density of the present (hot rolled) steel is about 6.80 g/cm³, about 13% lower than pure Fe (b0016, b0076).

Lattice parameters obtained from XRD profiles: the lattice parameter of α phase changes in the range 2.89–2.91 Å, of γ phase in the range 3.65–3.67 Å, and of κ-carbide in the range 3.76–3.79 Å (b0027).
The lattices of α and γ phase (the main phase constituents) are slightly expanded by Mn, Al and C atoms, which contributes to the low density of the steel (b0027).
The hot-rolled plate was produced with a thickness of 3 mm, with a finishing rolling temperature around 880 °C, and then water quenched to about 300 °C (b0015).
This hot-rolled + water-quenched plate (HR) is the common precursor/reference state for all subsequent annealing treatments (700–1200 °C for 1 h) studied in the paper (b0015, figure_001).
